initialize.instructions: Use project_create_blank for a blank game or project_create for a sample. Select the project before editing. In Hermes, show a successful playable build to the user early with chromatic_present_game (the hermretro emulator beside the chat); if the user cannot see that emulator, open studio.playerUrl from its result with desktop_preview, never web_preview URLs. Defer updates that could interrupt human play, saves or recordings; resolve unknown outcomes first. Do not arbitrarily reload or autoplay. Continue gameplay headlessly with public PyBoy emulator_run on the intended exact ROM, then emulator_step and emulator_observe; use emulator_review for retained evidence. Browser access is not a prerequisite for gameplay checks. If PyBoy is missing, follow the setup skill for the emulator component within existing authorization. Keep denials and uncertain actions scoped; never replay them. Native gameplay does not verify browser UI, annotations or physical capture. Use device_capture to watch physical play beside the chat in Hermes Desktop; emulator controls cannot drive hardware. Inspect the exact ROM before an approved device action. Close only temporary sessions you own when no longer needed, preserving user play and recordings.

tools.name: session_status
tools.title: Inspect native game session
tools.description: Report explicit project selection, authorized workspace identity, selection generation, and active emulator state without authorizing or modifying files.

tools.name: project_discover
tools.title: Discover native game project
tools.description: Inspect the explicitly selected native game project, or discover a supplied path inside the already authorized workspace without changing selection.

tools.name: project_select
tools.title: Select native game project
tools.description: Select the project to inspect or edit. Without a configured workspace, supply its absolute path; otherwise stay within the authorized workspace. The bundled starter requires allowStarter; active emulators or mutations prevent switching.

tools.name: project_create
tools.title: Create an editable native game project
tools.description: Create an editable project from starter or the optional Wrecklight source sample. If Wrecklight is not bundled, supply its matching local templateSourcePath. The source is verified and never modified. With no workspace configured, use an absolute new destination under an existing canonical parent; otherwise stay within the workspace. Select only when requested.

tools.name: project_create_blank
tools.title: Create a blank game project
tools.description: Create a new editable project with one empty Start scene and original minimal resources, without sample quests, actors or triggers. Configure its native game type and color mode; defaults are TOPDOWN and color. The destination must be new: use an absolute path under an existing parent when no workspace is configured, otherwise stay within the authorized workspace. Select only when requested. No compiler or emulator is required.

colorMode.description: mono: monochrome; mixed: color with monochrome compatibility; color: color-only.

tools.name: project_inspect
tools.title: Inspect native game project
tools.description: Read the selected native game project's metadata, settings, format, and project health without changing files.

tools.name: project_inventory
tools.title: Find and inventory project resources
tools.description: Find scenes, actors, assets and other resources by name or stable ID, or list them with standard detail (up to 50 per page by default). Narrow by resource type; use nextCursor with the same filters for another page.

query.description: Case-insensitive literal substring of resource names, IDs, or asset filenames (not diagnostics). Applies before pagination; reuse with nextCursor. Normalized layout only.

detail.description: Default standard. Use summary for IDs and names; full includes resource detail.

cursor.description: Pass the preceding result's nextCursor with the same filters. Reinspect if the cursor becomes stale.

tools.name: project_refresh
tools.title: Strongly refresh indexed project state
tools.description: Perform an explicitly requested authoritative authored-project verification and publish fresh indexed revision, semantic generation, and bounded telemetry without modifying project files.

tools.name: scene_create
tools.title: Create native game scene
tools.description: Create one native scene in the selected distributed or legacy native game project.

tools.name: scene_update
tools.title: Update native game scene
tools.description: Update an existing scene by stable scene ID while preserving other project resources.

tools.name: actor_create
tools.title: Create native game actor
tools.description: Create an actor in an existing scene, optionally assigning a sprite, facing direction, tile position within the scene, and dialogue.

x.description: Tile X coordinate inside the selected scene.

y.description: Tile Y coordinate inside the selected scene.

tools.name: dialogue_update
tools.title: Update scene, actor, or trigger dialogue
tools.description: Update scene, actor, or trigger dialogue; omit actorId and triggerId for the scene. Without eventId, updates the first recursive EVENT_TEXT or creates one. Use expectedRevision from script_inspect to guard the owner resource.

eventId.description: Exact dialogue event ID; omit to update the first recursive EVENT_TEXT or create one if none exists.

expectedRevision.description: Exact owner-resource revision from script_inspect for this scene, actor, or trigger; use the result revision to guard another update.

tools.name: settings_update
tools.title: Update game settings
tools.description: Update project color, cartridge, music, player start position, direction and move speed, player sprite, palette, or compiler settings. Optional expectedRevision checks the current project before writing.

startMoveSpeed.description: Player move speed in pixels per frame in TOPDOWN, SHMUP and POINTNCLICK scenes: GB Studio offers 0.25, 0.5, 1 (default), 2, 3 and 4. PLATFORM scenes use the plat_* engine fields and ADVENTURE scenes adv_walk_vel and adv_run_vel (engine_field_update).

tools.name: graphics_analyze
tools.title: Analyze Game Boy pixel art
tools.description: Inspect a real project PNG for dimensions, distinct/flipped tiles, 15-bit GBC colors, palette families, quantization, viewport usage, hardware budgets, and precise violations.

tools.name: web_build
tools.title: Build the official native game browser export
tools.description: Compile the selected native game project with the official make:web command, preserving its genuine Binjgb/WebAssembly browser emulator and reusing a verified export when authored project inputs have not changed.

outputPath.description: Export directory relative to the selected project; defaults to build/web.

timeoutMs.description: Time allowed for the official export, in milliseconds.

force.description: Rebuild instead of reusing an unchanged, verified export.

cacheOnly.description: Use only an unchanged, verified export; refuse instead of compiling on a cache miss.

tools.name: web_preview
tools.title: Preview a game and capture or reopen saved moments
tools.description: Open or refresh the selected project's official player (the engine's own preview). To show the game to the user in Hermes, call chromatic_present_game instead (it shows the game in the hermretro emulator); do not open this URL yourself. If the user says they cannot see that emulator, open studio.playerUrl from chromatic_present_game's result with desktop_preview (action "open"). If unavailable, locked or unreachable, keep the URL and state and report the browser limitation; do not launch an external browser. Continue gameplay with public PyBoy emulator_run on the intended exact ROM, then emulator_step/emulator_observe; browser UI and annotation checks remain unverified. Preview URLs are process-local and can expire after plugin restart or a fresh chat. On connection refused, inspect action status; if no live preview exists, select the original project and open again, using the newly returned URL without forcing a rebuild. Do not infer browser-policy failure from connection refused. Preserve unresolved old saves/recordings and explicit access refusals. Reuse only the current active URL for the same task; preserve user play and recording. outputPath, timeoutMs and force apply only to open. Other actions use the already-open player: status lists views, list_states returns saved IDs, and capture_state or restore_state pauses the selected view. Saved states require the exact build; native edits require a rebuild. Input holds ordinary game buttons in the running browser only, with exact status binding, at most 2 seconds. Human input cancels it. Timed video uses start_recording, recording_status, stop_recording and read_capture with the same visible UI recorder. Keep the player open until saved and acknowledged. For an expired URL use action recover on the same project: it only reopens a verified export, never rebuilds or restores unsaved state. No implicit resume or replay; inspect status after uncertainty.

outputPath.description: Open only: project-relative export directory; defaults to build/web.

timeoutMs.description: Open only: time allowed for the official export, in milliseconds.

force.description: Open only: rebuild instead of reusing an unchanged, verified export.

cacheOnly.description: Use only an unchanged, verified export; refuse instead of compiling on a cache miss.

action.description: Default open. Recover reopens a verified existing export without rebuilding. State commands control the already-open player.

viewId.description: For capture_state or restore_state: use a player ID from status when more than one browser view is open.

installationBinding.description: dismiss_install_failure only: exact generation/requestId/operationId from install_status. Explicitly acknowledges the known-closed failed attempt without erasing evidence or writing a cartridge; fresh selection and confirmation are still required.

installationRequestId.description: install_status only: original preview request ID. When supplied, return only that request with no fallback; when omitted, return the latest manual request. Match the returned request ID and generation before adopting its result.

stateId.description: For restore_state only: required saved state ID from list_states.

binding.description: Input only: copy the exact listener, player, build and input generation from status.

buttons.description: Input only: unique ordinary game buttons, with no opposing directions. Empty observes a neutral interval.

durationMs.description: Input only: wall-clock hold, 250 ms by default; not exact frames.

recordingBinding.description: Start recording only: exact listener, view, build and recording generation from status.

recordingDurationMs.description: Start recording only: fixed duration, 180000 ms by default; at most 600000 ms.

recordingId.description: Original job ID for recording_status, stop_recording or read_capture. Never retry an uncertain start.

tools.name: device_capture
tools.title: Capture the physical Chromatic USB video feed
tools.description: Open the selected project's physical Chromatic feed for the user to watch. In Hermes Desktop, open the returned URL beside the chat with the desktop_preview tool (action "open"); without that tool, give the user the URL. If unavailable, keep the URL and report the blocker without external-browser fallback. Supports macOS and Linux (x64/ARM64); Windows device capture is unavailable. The browser displays native frames and never requests camera or microphone access. On macOS, the user explicitly enables capture in Connection settings and grants normal OS access; tools cannot silently enable it. Optional macOS USB audio must match the same player. On Linux, connect with no Enable step or macOS permission prompt; capture is video-only. list_devices returns exact choices and diagnostic counts; Linux listing briefly opens matching nodes for capabilities without streaming, while macOS listing is passive. permission_status reports platform access state; open_settings opens Connection settings. connect requires inventoryId and exact selection from that list, valid for 60 seconds. start_recording returns a capture ID and deadline (3 minutes default, 10 minutes maximum, 128 MiB); poll status with captureId. Browser visibility does not stop recording. live_frame returns the latest native preview; screenshot saves PNG. read_capture returns the last two frame IDs, a saved screenshot or completed recording (latest by default). stop_recording finalizes 8x integer-upscaled video and keeps the live stream connected; disconnect releases the device. Reuse the active URL; close only owned temporary sessions after user play and saves finish. Do not replay uncertain commands. Native labels and samples do not authenticate the cartridge ROM or prove game FPS.

diagnosticTrace.description: For open only: opt in to bounded service/browser stage evidence before connecting; an existing session must be disconnected and idle to change it.

includeTrace.description: For status only: return the bounded diagnostic trace when explicitly requested.

tools.name: web_preview_close
tools.title: Close the active native game browser preview
tools.description: Stop this plugin instance's local authenticated browser-preview server and invalidate its capability URL without deleting the cached export. Close task-owned temporary previews when finished; preserve a user's ongoing or paused game and unresolved recording/save.

tools.name: rom_build
tools.title: Build an actual Game Boy ROM
tools.description: Build the selected native game project with the official CLI by default, or compile standalone C with GBDK. Supply only one input path. A project build also captures the debug artifacts emulator_run uses for source debugging, so emulator_debug works on the ROM it returns; pass the returned outputPath to rom_inspect or emulator_run.

projectPath.description: Omit to build the selected .gbsproj. An override must stay within that project; do not combine with sourcePath.

sourcePath.description: Standalone .c source inside the authorized workspace; incompatible with projectPath and debug artifact capture.

outputPath.description: Optional .gb or .gbc output, relative to the selected project for native project builds or to the authorized workspace for standalone C.

captureDebugArtifacts.description: Project builds default to true: matching symbols (about 30 KB in build/<rom>.debug) for emulator_run's source debugging; false skips them. Not for standalone C builds.

detail.description: compact (default) reports the debug artifacts' folder and whether source debugging is available; full adds their files, hashes and the build identity.

tools.name: rom_inspect
tools.title: Inspect a real cartridge ROM
tools.description: Inspect a .gb or .gbc file, including standalone ROMs inside an authorized workspace; no native game project is required when GB_STUDIO_WORKSPACE_ROOT is configured. Read its exact size and SHA-256, cartridge header, title, color support, mapper, ROM/RAM capacities, Nintendo logo, checksums, and validation status. Use the returned path, sizeBytes, and sha256 to bind Chromatic play or flash to this exact ROM.

romPath.description: Relative to the authorized workspace, or an absolute path inside it. Without a workspace, select the containing native game project first. Never select a standalone ROM as a project.

tools.name: toolchain_prepare
tools.title: Prepare missing game tools
tools.description: Prepare compiler or local emulator dependencies using the installed plugin's managed setup. Use for an authorized build/play request when toolchain_doctor reports missing dependencies. Does not install or register plugins, install device drivers, or activate hardware. Reuses setup-owned components and preserves configured roots and installer locks. Inspect an incomplete result; never blindly retry a refusal. After success continue the original build/preview in this session.

tools.name: toolchain_doctor
tools.title: Check local game tooling
tools.description: Passively inspect compatible dependency metadata and task readiness for the bound runtime/toolchain. Optional named probes explicitly execute CLI --version, GBDK -v, or isolated emulator imports; no ROM is loaded and metadata readiness is separate from probe health.

tasks.description: Optional readiness filters; omit for the default task set.

probes.description: Omit for passive metadata only; each named probe explicitly runs a local dependency check.

tools.name: emulator_run
tools.title: Run an actual GB/GBC ROM
tools.description: Start or reuse an isolated headless PyBoy session for the intended genuine ROM. Use it for gameplay checks even when the browser is unavailable, locked or unreachable; no browser session is required. If PyBoy is missing, follow the setup skill's emulator component. Continue with emulator_step/emulator_observe and use emulator_review for retained evidence. Unchanged ROMs retain their live frame and controller state; recording starts a clean bounded recorded boot. Source debugging (emulator_debug) is on when rom_build captured debug artifacts for this exact ROM in this session. This does not verify browser UI or drive physical hardware.

romPath.description: Use the exact cartridge path returned by rom_build or rom_inspect.

cgb.description: On a fresh boot, omit to follow the cartridge default; false forces monochrome DMG, true requests color hardware.

initialFrames.description: Frames to advance on a fresh boot only; defaults to 120. Reusing a running ROM does not advance it.

restart.description: Set true for an intentional fresh boot; otherwise an unchanged ROM reuses its current frame and inputs.

recording.description: Use an options object (including {}) for a fresh recorded boot; omit or use false to leave recording off for a new boot.

debugMode.description: Omit for source when rom_build captured debug artifacts for this exact cartridge in this session, else rom; source requires them; rom turns source debugging off.

tools.name: emulator_replay
tools.title: Replay a recorded attempt on a ROM
tools.description: Boot a ROM, usually one rom_build just rebuilt, the way a recorded attempt booted and play that attempt's inputs again in one call, comparing every frame with the attempt's (coverage:'retained-frames' when an older recording kept only its sampled images). Use it after each rebuild instead of replaying a route by hand. By default the replay stops at the first frame that differs and returns the recorded and replayed images; onDivergence:'continue' plays every input and reports the first difference; toActionIndex replays only up to that action (a recordingSpan's toActionIndex). A replay that starts ends the current session (a refused one leaves it running); the new session stays open where the replay ended, with the last recorded buttons still held, and is recorded as a new attempt (recording:false records nothing), so emulator_step, checkpoints and review continue from there. A cartridge with a real-time clock replays best effort (deterministic:false). Images are the source's retained frame (expected, when it kept one there), the replay's frame at the difference (actual) and the final frame (end). replay.endedSession names the session it ended (with its recording, which it finished when still recording). expect asks for a verdict in the same call (passed, failed, or needs-review when the scene or variables could not be read), and finishRecording stops the replay's recording with that verdict as its outcome, also in the same call, so no other call can come between.

romPath.description: The ROM to replay on: the exact cartridge path returned by rom_build or rom_inspect.

recordingPath.description: The recorded attempt to replay; defaults to the source of a replay that stopped before the end of its route, else the current or most recent recording.

sessionId.description: The attempt's sessionId: the replay is refused, leaving the current session running, when recordingPath holds another attempt.

branchId.description: The attempt's branch to replay; defaults to its current branch.

toActionIndex.description: Replay the attempt's actions up to and including this index, such as a recordingSpan's toActionIndex; defaults to all of them.

onDivergence.description: stop (default) ends the replay at the first frame that differs; continue plays every input anyway.

recording.description: The replay is recorded with the source attempt's limits; an options object overrides them; false records nothing.

frames.description: match (default): a frame that differs from the recording fails; ignore: only the scene and variables decide (replay with onDivergence:'continue').

scene.description: The scene's name or symbol where the replay ends, read in source debug mode.

variables.description: Up to 8 variable names or symbols and their values where the replay ends, read in source debug mode.

expect.description: What the replay must end in; the result's verdict judges it.

finishRecording.description: true stops the replay's recording where it ended, with the verdict as its outcome; needs a recorded replay.

debugMode.description: Omit for source when rom_build captured debug artifacts for this exact cartridge in this session, else rom; source requires them; rom turns source debugging off.

includeImages.description: Set false to receive the report without images.

scale.description: Enlarge returned images 1–4× with square pixels; image hashes stay those of the native frames.

colorCorrection.description: none (default) returns the emulator's colors; chromatic shows color-hardware frames with the hermretro player's color correction, an approximation of the Chromatic's screen. A monochrome session, including a dual-mode cartridge run as DMG, keeps the emulator's colors. Sample hashes stay those of the native frames.

tools.name: emulator_step
tools.title: Play exact frames and observe the result
tools.description: Hold exact button sets for exact native frames and return genuine sampled PNGs. Give buttons and frames for one held set, or inputs for an ordered sequence run in this one call (at most 64 inputs, 3,600 frames and 8 samples in all): send a press, wait and press again as one inputs list, not as repeated identical calls. Each set is complete: buttons persist after the call, the same set does not release/repress them, and [] is neutral. Nothing advances between calls. By default the last frame is sampled and the result is compact; ask for more samples with sampleCount or sample:true, larger images with scale, or every field with detail:'full'. Optional imageLayout:'contact-sheet' lays out the SAME samples with frame/input labels, adding no steps or captures. Errors separate confirmed execution from image delivery: never repeat input merely to recover an image. To look without advancing, use emulator_observe. After emulator_recording stop, steps are refused until emulator_run boots again or emulator_replay, given the recordingPath and branchId stop returned, continues from the recording. colorCorrection:'chromatic' shows color-hardware frames as the Chromatic does.

buttons.description: With frames, for one held set: the complete set of held buttons; [] is neutral.

frames.description: With buttons: native frames to advance, at least 1. To look without advancing, use emulator_observe.

sampleCount.description: With buttons and frames: evenly spaced samples ending on the last frame, at least 1; defaults to 1. For no images, set includeImages:false.

buttons.description: The complete set of held buttons for this input; [] is neutral.

frames.description: Native frames to hold this set, at least 1.

sample.description: Also sample this input's last frame; the last input is always sampled.

inputs.description: Instead of buttons and frames: ordered inputs run in this one call, at most 3,600 frames and 8 samples in all. Press, wait, press again: [{buttons:['a'],frames:2},{buttons:[],frames:30},{buttons:['a'],frames:2}].

scale.description: Enlarge returned images 1–4× with square pixels (contact sheets default to 2×); sample hashes stay those of the native frames.

colorCorrection.description: none (default) returns the emulator's colors; chromatic shows color-hardware frames with the hermretro player's color correction, an approximation of the Chromatic's screen. A monochrome session, including a dual-mode cartridge run as DMG, keeps the emulator's colors. Sample hashes stay those of the native frames.

detail.description: compact (default): frame, buttons, samples and recordingSpan. full returns every field the engine reports, such as the ROM, runtime, clock, recording state and retained sample paths.

tools.name: emulator_observe
tools.title: Observe the current genuine framebuffer
tools.description: Return the current real 160×144 framebuffer and frame/input metadata without advancing frames, changing controller state, writing files, or appending recording events. Optional scale enlarges the image; imageLayout:'contact-sheet' labels that same image in memory; the individual PNG remains the default. The result is compact unless detail:'full'. It accepts no actions. Applied input and last-sampled input are reported separately. colorCorrection:'chromatic' shows color-hardware frames as the Chromatic does. Use emulator_step to play.

scale.description: Enlarge returned images 1–4× with square pixels (contact sheets default to 2×); sample hashes stay those of the native frames.

colorCorrection.description: none (default) returns the emulator's colors; chromatic shows color-hardware frames with the hermretro player's color correction, an approximation of the Chromatic's screen. A monochrome session, including a dual-mode cartridge run as DMG, keeps the emulator's colors. Sample hashes stay those of the native frames.

detail.description: compact (default): frame, buttons, samples and recordingSpan. full returns every field the engine reports, such as the ROM, runtime, clock, recording state and retained sample paths.

tools.name: emulator_inspect
tools.title: Inspect bounded emulator state
tools.description: Read hardware OAM or bounded memory (up to 2,048 bytes) without advancing frames. The memory and vram views require region, offset and length; vram accepts only region:'vram'. visibleOnly, limit and includeScanlineSummary apply only to the oam view. For variables, scene names, actor positions or dialogue state, use emulator_debug.

view.description: oam reads hardware sprite objects; memory and vram read a bounded byte range.

visibleOnly.description: oam only: filter out objects not visible on screen.

limit.description: oam only: maximum objects to return.

includeScanlineSummary.description: oam only: include peak sprite count, peak scanlines, and the count of scanlines over the hardware limit.

region.description: Required for memory and vram; the vram view requires region vram.

offset.description: Required for memory and vram: zero-based byte offset within the region, not an absolute CPU address.

length.description: Required for memory and vram: byte count; the full range must fit within the region.

bank.description: memory/vram only: optional for VRAM (0–1) or WRAM (0–7). A banked WRAM range must fit within 4 KiB.

tools.name: emulator_audio
tools.title: Check which sound channels the game drives
tools.description: Read the Game Boy sound hardware's registers on the current frame without advancing. active is true when the sound hardware is on and a channel (pulse1, pulse2, wave, noise) is enabled, its DAC on and sent to a speaker; each channel reports active, enabled, dac, panned, and startVolume (pulse and noise envelope start, 0–15) or outputLevel (wave). Registers show what the game drives, not what comes out: a pulse or noise note whose envelope has faded stays active until the next note or cut. This is one frame: check a short sound effect on the frames just after it starts. A song keeps its channels active between notes.

tools.name: emulator_status
tools.title: Inspect active emulator state
tools.description: With a ROM open, report its identity, native frame count, paused clock, execution time, recording limits, screen size, and held buttons without advancing. To check whether an emulator is active without starting a worker, use session_status and read emulatorActive.

tools.name: emulator_close
tools.title: Close active emulator session
tools.description: Cancel queued or in-flight play/build work, retain recording evidence, stop the isolated worker, and wait for cleanup. Safe to repeat; never deletes prior attempts.

tools.name: emulator_review
tools.title: Review committed recorded inputs and sampled frames
tools.description: Review a recorded input interval (fromActionIndex,toActionIndex] using the recordingSpan returned by emulator_step. Returns verified retained samples, known physical input-delivery records, pins, missing endpoints and sampling gaps; never captures or advances play. Empty intervals and post-close reads are supported. Maximum 3,600 native frames, 4,096 actions, and 2 MiB metadata. Integrity does not establish a gameplay outcome.

recordingPath.description: Optional recording directory; use the path returned when recording began or omit for the current/recent recording.

branchId.description: Exact branchId from the same recordingSpan.

fromActionIndex.description: Exclusive normalized start boundary from recordingSpan; equal bounds request an empty interval.

toActionIndex.description: Inclusive normalized end boundary from the same recordingSpan.

fromFrame.description: Optional with toFrame; both must match the selected normalized action boundaries.

toFrame.description: Optional with fromFrame; both must match the selected normalized action boundaries.

prefixPin.description: Optional exact prefixPin returned in recordingSpan; protects the reviewed journal prefix.

maxImages.description: Maximum returned real samples; defaults to four.

includeImages.description: Set false to receive metadata without inline images in either layout.

imageLayout.description: Individual images are the default; contact-sheet labels the same samples in memory without new captures or file writes.

tools.name: emulator_checkpoint
tools.title: Save or branch from an opaque checkpoint
tools.description: Save a paused, neutral, sampled state or restore it into the same ROM and runtime: the exact ROM, or a rebuild of the unchanged project. Saving needs an active recording (emulator_run with recording:{}, not yet stopped) and a sampled neutral frame: no held buttons, and the last emulator_step ended with buttons:[] for at least one frame, such as a final input {buttons:[],frames:1}. Restoring preserves the original attempt and starts a new recorded branch; incompatible or stale states fail before loading.

checkpointId.description: Restore only; required checkpointId returned by save.

recordingPath.description: Restore only; optional directory containing the original recording and checkpoint.

label.description: Save only; an optional label for the new checkpoint.

tools.name: emulator_recording
tools.title: Inspect, finish, archive or retrieve a recorded attempt
tools.description: Inspect/export history, stop the active recording, or archive/retrieve/restore it. stop finalizes the recording and ends its session: steps, input and checkpoints are refused until emulator_run boots again (restart:true, or recording:{} to record), and emulator_replay with the recordingPath and branchId stop returns continues from where it ended (it reached the end when replay.replayedActions equals replay.source.actionCount). access_diagnostic takes only action; without a worker, lease, recording read or process probe, it cannot prove liveness or authorize recovery. Maintenance requires closed transports and exclusive client access. Archive moves unchanged bytes in the project, preserves original-path mapping and releases admission reservation, not disk space. Retrieval verifies provenance without an emulator; restore reinstates quota.

recordingPath.description: Required and the only other input for archive/retrieve/restore; optional for status/export; do not pass for stop or access_diagnostic.

branchId.description: Export only; select a recorded branch. Omit to use the current/default branch.

actionOffset.description: Export action offset; use nextActionOffset for the next page. This does not page evidence.

limit.description: Export returns up to 64 actions by default and the latest min(limit, 32) evidence samples. Check counts and truncation for omissions.

outcome.description: Stop only; optional assessment when finalizing the active recording.

reason.description: Stop only; optional explanation for the active recording's outcome.

tools.name: emulator_clip
tools.title: Extract a supporting playtest clip
tools.description: Extract a GIF from genuine retained recorded frames without reopening or advancing a ROM. Restore maintenance-archived recordings first with emulator_recording. Requires exact retained endpoints, at most 600 selected frame occurrences and 60 seconds of native game time. Sparse samples are held, never interpolated; output never overwrites files. Returns source/output timing, gaps and digest.

outputPath.description: New .gif path inside the recording directory or the authorized artifacts directory.

recordingPath.description: Optional retained or restored recording directory; maintenance archives must be restored first.

branchId.description: Optional recorded branch to use for the source frames.

startFrame.description: Inclusive start for one interval; do not combine with cuts.

endFrame.description: Inclusive end for one interval; do not combine with cuts.

cuts.description: One to 16 ordered inclusive intervals; repeats are preserved. Do not combine with top-level startFrame or endFrame.

tools.name: emulator_debug
tools.title: Inspect authenticated author state
tools.description: Read the current scene, variable values, live state and authored collision tiles and references while paused. live reports the player (and named actors) tile and pixel position, direction, moving and moveSpeed (scripted moves and top-down walking; a platformer player reports platform state and velocities in pixels per frame instead), withheld while sceneLoading; ui: overlayOpen, dialogue (none, drawing, waiting, menu or unknown) and the buttons the script that owns input accepts next; scripts: running count and whether the VM is locked. Works on a ROM rom_build built in this session (it captures debug artifacts by default) once emulator_run starts it. Rejects stale source/artifacts or different ROM bytes; unavailable in ROM-only mode.

variableNames.description: Authored variable names or symbols: an exact match first, then the full name or symbol in any case, then the symbol without var_ (has_oil). Ambiguous names list their IDs. Omit both variable lists for every variable.

actors.description: Current-scene actors to report live, by authored name, ID or symbol, or 'all'. The player is always reported.

referenceLimit.description: Authored references to the scene and selected variables; defaults to 0 (compact) or 16 (full).

detail.description: compact (default): frame, scene, live state, variables and what you ask for. full adds the build identity, the standing limitations and references.

tools.name: tilemap_atlas_create
tools.title: Register a reusable tile atlas
tools.description: Register project-owned opaque indexed 8x8 source tiles and sparse named motifs. Source PNG and atlas paths stay under project/tilemaps; no native room is changed.

tools.name: tilemap_create
tools.title: Create an additive native room recipe
tools.description: Explicitly capture an existing room's exact named atlas patterns or fill a new fixed-size background, retain the predecessor, and rebind only the selected scene. No automatic resize or approximated capture.

tools.name: tilemap_inspect
tools.title: Inspect tilemap source and native binding
tools.description: Strongly verify a room recipe or atlas and return bounded tile identities, exact 8x8 row-major RGBA pixelsSha256 hashes, native hashes and current project revision. Supply both recipePath and atlasPath to inspect that verified room's bound atlas, including an explicitly adopted legacy atlas. Atlas-only inspection retains path-derived identity checks. This is authored-source evidence.

tools.name: tilemap_edit
tools.title: Apply bounded native room edits
tools.description: Edit a revision-bound recipe. Place/fill/stamp operates outside protected cells. Exclusive replace_cells changes selected pixels/palettes and preserves collisions; exclusive set_collision_cells changes only selected collision bytes and synchronizes the scene. Both require exact pixel/palette/collision preimages and preserve protection lists and unselected cells, including when selecting protected cells. Replacement atlases must preserve existing meanings. Exclusive adopt_binding validates six file preimages and registers retained identities without changing native files or cells. Dependency guards and best-effort rollback apply; no generic override.

tools.name: tilemap_compile
tools.title: Verify deterministic native room regeneration
tools.description: Recompile an unchanged room recipe, retaining native IDs and identical bytes. Refuse drifted atlas/native outputs or shared background users; never overwrite a newer external edit.

tools.name: scene_inspect
tools.title: Inspect one scene
tools.description: Read a scene and up to 25 actors and 25 triggers. Returns project revision for scene_apply/delete and exact sceneRevision for trigger_create or scene-owned script edits. Scripts are omitted by default; use script_inspect for one event or branch. Check truncated for omissions.

tools.name: scene_delete
tools.title: Delete a scene
tools.description: Delete an unreferenced scene, or use dryRun to preview. Guard with scene_inspect.revision (the whole-project revision).

expectedRevision.description: Whole-project revision from scene_inspect.revision or project_inspect.revision.

tools.name: scene_apply
tools.title: Apply a bounded scene transaction
tools.description: Apply 1–100 ordered scene, actor, trigger, event, collision, or variable edits. Guard with scene_inspect.revision; dryRun previews without writing. Distributed projects have best-effort rollback, not cross-file atomicity.

expectedRevision.description: Whole-project revision from scene_inspect.revision or project_inspect.revision; resource revisions are not interchangeable.

tools.name: actor_inspect
tools.title: Inspect actor
tools.description: Read one scene actor and its current resource revision without modifying the project.

tools.name: actor_update
tools.title: Update actor
tools.description: Update one existing actor's position, sprite, facing direction, or editable metadata.

tools.name: actor_delete
tools.title: Delete actor
tools.description: Delete one unreferenced actor without changing unrelated scene or script resources.

tools.name: trigger_inspect
tools.title: Inspect trigger
tools.description: Read one scene trigger, its bounds, scripts, and stable resource revision.

tools.name: trigger_create
tools.title: Create trigger
tools.description: Create a bounded native scene trigger without replacing existing resources. Guard with scene_inspect.sceneRevision.

expectedRevision.description: Exact scene resource revision: use scene_inspect.sceneRevision, not its whole-project revision.

tools.name: trigger_update
tools.title: Update trigger
tools.description: Update an existing trigger's name, position, dimensions, or editable properties.

tools.name: trigger_delete
tools.title: Delete trigger
tools.description: Delete one unreferenced trigger while preserving unrelated gameplay resources.

tools.name: asset_import
tools.title: Import an image or audio asset
tools.description: Register project-local PNGs, music and sound effects as native assets: one with assetPath and kind, or up to 32 in assets (all or none). Music is a hUGETracker .uge or a four-channel .mod; a sound is a .wav (up to about 3.6 s) or a Game Boy .vgm/.vgz. The tool checks an audio file, writes its sidecar with an ID that stays the same, and returns a playEvent (EVENT_MUSIC_PLAY or EVENT_SOUND_PLAY_EFFECT) to add to a script; to write music from notes, use music_compose. Sprite profiles: static 16x16, directional 48x16, directional_animated 96x16, metasprite (a row of frameWidth x frameHeight frames, e.g. 32x32, built from 8x16 tiles), template. sprite.paletteIndex picks the scene sprite palette slot (0-7) for every tile. Generated profiles need the project's 8x16 sprite mode. A metasprite's collision box covers its whole frame; TOPDOWN sprites (sprite.sceneType, default the project's default scene type) on a 16 px top-down grid get a 16x16 box from the 16-pixel profiles. Each result includes the graphics analysis (status, tile budget as GB Studio compiles it, violations). native_metadata imports a complete sprite PNG/JSON pair: requires sourcePath, sprite.metadataPath, sourceSha256, metadataSha256 and a fresh whole-project expectedRevision. It creates only new outputs, supports dryRun, and returns the complete deterministic ID map with detail:'full'. Source paths stay inside the selected project. Actor rebinding is a separate guarded operation; do not replay an uncertain import.

assetPath.description: Destination: a PNG under assets/backgrounds or assets/sprites, a .uge or .mod under assets/music, or a .wav, .vgm or .vgz under assets/sounds. Required with kind unless assets is given.

paletteIndex.description: Scene sprite palette slot (0-7) every tile uses in color mode; defaults to 0.

frameWidth.description: metasprite only: frame width, a multiple of 8.

frameHeight.description: metasprite only: frame height, a multiple of 16; the PNG is one row of frames this tall.

sceneType.description: Scene type the sprite is for, e.g. TOPDOWN or PLATFORM; defaults to the project's default scene type. TOPDOWN on a 16 px top-down grid gives the 16-pixel profiles a 16x16 collision box.

assets.description: Import several assets in one call instead of the single-asset fields; all are checked before any is written. native_metadata is not allowed here.

expectedRevision.description: Required whole-project revision for native_metadata only.

dryRun.description: Validate the complete native_metadata import without publishing; defaults false.

detail.description: compact (default) returns each asset's id, paths and analysis; full adds a native_metadata import's ID map and pattern accounting.

tools.name: asset_inspect
tools.title: Inspect an asset
tools.description: Read a native background, sprite, song or sound and its sidecar metadata. Provide assetId or assetPath; if both are supplied, they must identify the same asset.

tools.name: music_compose
tools.title: Write a song
tools.description: Write an original song from note lists as a hUGETracker .uge under assets/music and register it with an ID that stays the same; returns the ID, the loop length and a playEvent (EVENT_MUSIC_PLAY) to add to a script. Give sections and an order, or bundled for a ready track. Channels: pulse1 (melody), pulse2 (harmony), wave (bass) and noise (drums). Each channel is a list of rows; a note rings until the next note or rest. Example section: {name:'A', pulse1:'C5:2 E5:2 G5:4 . -:3', wave:'C3:4 G2:4', noise:'kick:2 hat:2 snare:2 hat:2'}. Songs loop.

assetPath.description: Destination .uge under assets/music. Defaults to assets/music/<bundled>.uge for a bundled track.

bundled.description: Write a bundled original track instead of sections: bright-start (bouncy title), meadow-walk (easy overworld), cave-echo (slow minor dungeon), victory-lap (fanfare).

ticksPerRow.description: Frames (1/60 s) each row lasts; with 4 rows to a beat 6 is 150 BPM, 7 about 128 (default), 8 about 112, 10 about 90.

instruments.description: The song's instrument per channel (default pulse1 lead, pulse2 soft, wave bass); a section's channel can override it.

anyOf.description: Rows separated by spaces: a note in scientific pitch (C4, F#3, Bb5), . to rest, - to hold; :N makes a row last N rows (C4:4).

pulse1.description: A pulse channel's rows, C2–B7, or {notes, instrument} with lead, soft, pluck, square or thin.

pulse2.description: A pulse channel's rows, C2–B7, or {notes, instrument} with lead, soft, pluck, square or thin.

wave.description: The wave channel's rows, C1–B6, or {notes, instrument} with bass, mellow, saw or hollow.

noise.description: Drums: kick, snare, hat, . (rest) and - (hold), each with an optional :N.

sections.description: Named passages. A channel left out is silent; a shorter channel holds to the section's longest.

order.description: Section names in playing order, repeats allowed; defaults to each section once. The song loops back to the start.

overwrite.description: Replace the song already at assetPath, keeping its ID and every event that plays it.

tools.name: asset_update
tools.title: Update image asset
tools.description: Update native sidecar properties, or initialize replacement background palette assignments with copyTileColorsFrom and expectedRevision. Palette transfer preserves existing UI cells, requires equal dimensions, and supports dryRun.

tools.name: asset_delete
tools.title: Delete image asset
tools.description: Delete one unreferenced native image and its sidecar. Provide assetId or assetPath; if both are supplied, they must identify the same asset.

tools.name: native_graphics_update
tools.title: Update a supported native graphics atlas
tools.description: Apply inert atlas data to the supported wrecklight-title-v1 renderer only. Requires a whole-project expectedRevision and the complete current-header digest in the contract; dryRun previews. Preserves animation, attributes, font and credits. The contract path is informational, not a destination. Plugin files are outside the public project revision, so use the returned headerSha256 for the next preimage. This does not update dependency profiles or prove rendered output.

expectedRevision.description: Whole-project revision. The plugin header is separately guarded by currentHeader.sha256.

tools.name: sprite_inspect
tools.title: Inspect sprite animation
tools.description: Inspect genuine sprite states, animation slots, frame counts, object bounds, and optional bounded frame metadata.

tools.name: sprite_edit
tools.title: Update sprite metadata
tools.description: Update native sprite animation speed, collision bounds, state settings, or displayed name.

stateIndex.description: Existing state to update when setting flipLeft or animationType; defaults to 0.

tools.name: sprite_preview
tools.title: Preview authored sprite
tools.description: Write one labeled authored sprite frame, enlarged by default and optionally in a palette's sprite colors; this is not an emulator framebuffer. Omit outputPath for a unique capture, or supply a new PNG path.

scale.description: Integer enlargement; defaults to the largest that keeps the frame within 128 pixels.

paletteId.description: Draw the frame in this palette's sprite colors (entries 0, 1 and 3) instead of the source shades.

colorCorrection.description: none (default) writes the palette's exact colors; chromatic applies the color correction the hermretro player uses, an approximation of the Chromatic's screen.

tools.name: sprite_contact_sheet
tools.title: Preview sprite animation frames
tools.description: Write a labeled bounded sprite-source animation sheet, enlarged by default and optionally in a palette's sprite colors, without claiming genuine gameplay-frame provenance.

scale.description: Integer enlargement; defaults to the largest that keeps each frame within 64 pixels.

paletteId.description: Draw the frame in this palette's sprite colors (entries 0, 1 and 3) instead of the source shades.

colorCorrection.description: none (default) writes the palette's exact colors; chromatic applies the color correction the hermretro player uses, an approximation of the Chromatic's screen.

tools.name: palette_inspect
tools.title: Inspect project palettes
tools.description: Read one project-global four-color palette by paletteId, or list a bounded page. Returns the reserved UI palette and affected scene counts. Follow nextCursor to continue; if the project changes, restart without cursor.

paletteId.description: Exact palette ID. Returns one item in palettes; omit limit and cursor.

limit.description: Maximum palettes to list per page (default 250); the response byte limit can return fewer. Omit with paletteId.

cursor.description: Use the prior nextCursor to continue the same project listing. Omit with paletteId; restart without cursor after a project change.

tools.name: palette_create
tools.title: Create a color palette
tools.description: Create one genuine project-global Game Boy Color palette: four RGB colors, or three for a sprite palette.

colors.description: Four colors, lightest to darkest; or three for a sprite palette (lightest, middle, darkest), stored as entries 0, 1 and 3 because sprites never show entry 2. Three colors in an update keep the palette's entry 2.

tools.name: palette_update
tools.title: Update a color palette
tools.description: Update an existing shared palette while preserving authored default colors unless explicitly requested.

colors.description: Four colors, lightest to darkest; or three for a sprite palette (lightest, middle, darkest), stored as entries 0, 1 and 3 because sprites never show entry 2. Three colors in an update keep the palette's entry 2.

tools.name: palette_assign
tools.title: Assign scene palette
tools.description: Assign one actual background or object palette slot while protecting the reserved UI slot by default. A sprite slot returns the three colors sprites show and warns when entry 2 holds a color they never draw.

tools.name: palette_paint
tools.title: Paint background palette tiles
tools.description: Change native tile-color assignments on an unbound background without rewriting PNG pixels. For a background bound to a tilemap recipe, use tilemap_inspect then tilemap_edit replace_cells with unchanged pixel hashes; this direct tool does not update the recipe.

tools.name: graphics_analyze_scene
tools.title: Analyze scene graphics budgets
tools.description: Analyze authored background tiles, palette slots, sprite metadata, and engine/hardware budgets. Sprite usage estimates do not establish compiled allocation. Static actor scanline estimates exclude the player and do not establish simultaneous visibility; use emulator frames for runtime evidence.

tools.name: graphics_preview_scene
tools.title: Preview authored scene colors
tools.description: Write a static background color projection for sceneId, or an ordered contact sheet for 1–16 distinct sceneIds. Supply one form and a new PNG path; neither mode overwrites files. Output is enlarged 2x by default (magnification 1–4); columns apply only to sheets. colorCorrection chromatic approximates the Chromatic's display. Actors, UI, camera motion, and runtime gameplay are not shown.

colorCorrection.description: none (default) writes the palette's exact colors; chromatic applies the color correction the hermretro player uses, an approximation of the Chromatic's screen.

magnification.description: Integer enlargement; defaults to 2, or 1 when the enlarged image would be too large.

tools.name: script_inspect
tools.title: Inspect gameplay script
tools.description: Read one scene, actor, trigger, or nested event-branch script, named by sceneId with optional actorId, triggerId, scriptKey and branchPath (or the same fields as target). Returns its owner-resource revision for script_edit or script_transition; this differs from the project revision.

target.description: The same script as one object; give either target or sceneId with its optional actorId, triggerId, scriptKey and branchPath.

tools.name: script_edit
tools.title: Edit gameplay script event
tools.description: Insert, update, delete, or reorder one native event. Guard with script_inspect.revision for the same target; the returned revision can guard the next edit.

expectedRevision.description: Owner-resource revision returned by script_inspect for the same target, or the preceding successful script edit.

tools.name: script_transition
tools.title: Create a scene transition
tools.description: Insert a typed scene-switch event after checking its destination and coordinate bounds. Inspect destination collisions separately for passability. Guard with script_inspect.revision for the same source target.

expectedRevision.description: Owner-resource revision from script_inspect for the same source target.

tools.name: event_describe
tools.title: Describe GB Studio events
tools.description: Look up GB Studio's script events. With no arguments, list the categories; with query, category or includeDeprecated, list matching events (command, name, one-line summary; 40 at a time, nextCursor for more); with events, describe up to 5: every arg with its type, default, allowed values and the conditions under which it is used, child branches, warnings, deprecation with its replacement and how to convert, what the event needs first, and an example to adapt. Read from GB Studio's own event definitions; needs no project.

events.description: Up to 5 event commands to describe in full, e.g. ["EVENT_IF","EVENT_SET_VALUE"].

query.description: Words to find in an event's command, name, summary, category or arg names, e.g. sound or actor position.

category.description: A category from the listing, e.g. Actor, Dialogue & Menus or Uncategorized.

includeDeprecated.description: List deprecated events too (default false); alone, lists every event.

cursor.description: A listing's nextCursor, to list the matches after it.

detail.description: With events: compact leaves out descriptions and conditions (default full).

tools.name: variable_inspect
tools.title: Inspect named game variables
tools.description: Read authored global variable metadata and its resource revision. Use emulator_debug for live values; this tool does not read runtime memory.

variableId.description: Canonical nonnegative decimal string, e.g. 0 or 12: no leading zeros; maximum 9007199254740991. This is an authored ID, not an emulator memory address.

tools.name: variable_set
tools.title: Create or update a named variable
tools.description: Create or update an authored global variable. Provide a name for a new variable; omit its ID or symbol for automatic defaults, or supply a decimal ID and var_<identifier> symbol. Guard with variable_inspect.revision; this does not change live emulator memory.

variableId.description: Canonical nonnegative decimal string, e.g. 0 or 12: no leading zeros; maximum 9007199254740991. This is an authored ID, not an emulator memory address.

name.description: Required when creating a new variable; omit only to retain an existing name.

symbol.description: Optional compiler symbol, e.g. var_audit_counter. Must begin with var_ followed by an ASCII letter, then letters, digits or underscores. Omit to retain the existing symbol or generate one from a new variable's name.

expectedRevision.description: Variable-resource revision returned by variable_inspect or the preceding successful variable edit.

tools.name: variable_delete
tools.title: Delete a named variable
tools.description: Delete an unreferenced authored global variable; guard with variable_inspect.revision. Use world_dependencies if deletion is blocked. This does not change live emulator memory.

variableId.description: Canonical nonnegative decimal string, e.g. 0 or 12: no leading zeros; maximum 9007199254740991. This is an authored ID, not an emulator memory address.

expectedRevision.description: Variable-resource revision returned by variable_inspect or the preceding successful variable edit.

tools.name: engine_field_inspect
tools.title: Inspect native engine field overrides
tools.description: Read bounded native engine-field overrides, preserving numeric checkbox values and the resource's exact revision.

tools.name: engine_field_update
tools.title: Update native engine field overrides
tools.description: Safely update or append bounded native engine-field overrides with numeric checkbox validation and optional optimistic resource revisions.

tools.name: collision_inspect
tools.title: Inspect scene collision tiles
tools.description: Decode a bounded rectangular sample of the selected scene's actual hexadecimal collision grid.

tools.name: collision_edit
tools.title: Edit scene collision tiles
tools.description: Change bounded collision tiles or rectangles in an unbound scene. For a bound tilemap use tilemap_edit to synchronize its recipe. Untouched bytes stay intact; resetInvalid explicitly replaces a malformed grid with zeros before editing.

tools.name: dialogue_analyze
tools.title: Analyze authored dialogue fit
tools.description: Measure real selected-font glyph widths, explicit authored pages, dialogue-card layouts, overflow, and optional safe wrapping suggestions.

tools.name: dialogue_preview
tools.title: Preview authored dialogue
tools.description: Write a bounded native-size font-aware static dialogue preview explicitly labeled as not emulator or runtime verified.

tools.name: world_dependencies
tools.title: Inspect indexed gameplay dependencies
tools.description: Read gameplay relationships and semantic coverage without changing project files. Page references with cursor and coverage reasons with coverageCursor; both retain totals and generation-bound cursors within 32 KiB. Coverage can be incomplete because of unresolved native references or unsupported custom-event sources, authored contract, or invocation; compiling, retrying or adopting a tilemap cannot establish an unsupported custom-event contract.

tools.name: device
tools.title: Inspect Chromatic devices and operations
tools.description: Read platform/driver requirements without touching USB, list connected Chromatics, or retrieve an original operation. Supply a caller-chosen requestId for discovery so a lost reply can be recovered without scanning again; reusing it returns the original result, never fresh tokens. Choose the intended device; there is no default player. Report discovery diagnostics even when another device is selectable. Duplicate player numbers need distinct on-device settings followed by reconnection; unmatched USB functions need the reported access checks. For a lost or unresolved action, read its original operation_status; do not start a replacement.

command.description: status: no other fields; list_devices: optional requestId; operation_status: exactly one of operationId or requestId.

operationId.description: operation_status only: returned operation ID; omit requestId.

requestId.description: list_devices: optional caller-chosen ID for one discovery. operation_status: original discovery, setup, play, or flash request ID; omit operationId.

tools.name: setup
tools.title: Set up Chromatic device access
tools.description: Install drivers or detect a cartridge when the user requests that specific action. Driver setup changes Linux udev access or requests Windows administrator approval; macOS needs no vendor driver. Cartridge detection can reconfigure the FPGA and consumes the selected device token. Retain the requestId and poll device operation_status. Unreadable cartridges or unknown flash models return recovery guidance; do not automatically repeat detection.

command.description: install_drivers requires only sessionId; detect_cartridge requires only deviceToken. Both require requestId and confirm.

requestId.description: Unique ID for the authorized attempt. If the reply is lost, retrieve this same ID through device operation_status; it never starts another attempt.

confirm.description: Set true only when the user explicitly requests this specific setup, live-play, or write action.

sessionId.description: Required for install_drivers; use the sessionId from current device status.

deviceToken.description: Required for detect_cartridge; choose a token from current discovery. The action consumes it.

tools.name: flash
tools.title: Write a selected ROM to Chromatic
tools.description: Flash homebrew or the user's own game; refuse third-party commercial games, including known retail rebuilds. A ROM you compiled from game source otherwise qualifies; try the local emulator for unknown supplied ROMs and do not flash while origin remains unclear. Developer Mode activation is managed outside this plugin using ModRetro Updater: https://support.modretro.com/en_us/articles/chromatic-firmware-updater-ryhoYnzCx. Never request or accept activation codes. After external activation, use fresh device selection and normal flash confirmation; do not automatically retry an uncertain write. On the first flash per device, explain that existing cartridge game data will be erased, saves may be lost, and no backup is made; get explicit consent acknowledging this. Do not repeat consent for later writes the user requests on the same device. Requires a fresh selected deviceToken and the path, sizeBytes, and SHA-256 from rom_inspect. Poll device operation_status; use operationId for a copied preview error because its requestId is preview-scoped. device.program_failed alone does not identify the cause: inspect the original public error summary and recovery. Timeout, cancellation, or process closure never authorizes another flash. Vendor success does not establish manual boot, play, or audio.

deviceToken.description: Select this token from the latest device discovery; an accepted detect, play, or flash consumes it.

requestId.description: Unique ID for the authorized attempt. If the reply is lost, retrieve this same ID through device operation_status; it never starts another attempt.

confirm.description: Set true only for a user-requested write once the user has explicitly accepted cartridge data loss for this device.

tools.name: play
tools.title: Stream host emulation to Chromatic
tools.description: Stream timed host-emulated video/audio to the selected Chromatic; this does not write or run the cartridge. Requires a user-requested live demo, a fresh selected deviceToken, and the path, sizeBytes, and SHA-256 from rom_inspect. Poll device operation_status until the original process closes; progress alone is not completion. Read returned HID diagnostics without treating them as a driver probe or retry instruction. No remote input, frame capture, stop command, or hardware performance counters are exposed.

deviceToken.description: Select this token from the latest device discovery; an accepted detect, play, or flash consumes it.

durationSeconds.description: Requested emulation seconds; defaults to 60. Completion requires observing the original process close.

saveMode.description: Default none disables save loading/writing. Isolated reuses battery saves only for this exact ROM SHA-256 under the authorized root.

requestId.description: Unique ID for the authorized attempt. If the reply is lost, retrieve this same ID through device operation_status; it never starts another attempt.

confirm.description: Set true only when the user explicitly requests this specific setup, live-play, or write action.
